title_en: The Limb of the Salil (the Half-Hearted Devotee)
translit:
|| Ath Shri Salilka Ang ||18||

Salilpe sakut bhalo | je kabahuk pave par ||
Salil buda kichmen | Jivana jaisi jal bin nav ||1||
Salil bhagatkun Jivana | mat koy patiay ||
Kabahun sant sangat kare | kabahu sakutan mil jay ||2||
Hathi buda kichmen | nahin uthanki ash ||
Hath pakhere Jivana | bhavjal bude das ||3||
Kanbi kulman Jivana | vansh na dise koy ||
Dina das bhakti kare | ante fenhe hoy ||4||
Bharado bhagat nahi Jivana | Kanbi or Sonar ||
Adha dhundha hoyga | koe Sadguruke upkar ||5||
Salil sakutan brahmanan | so khade bhelabhel ||
Yun bane nahi Jivana | jyun erandiyu fulel ||6||

|| Sakhi bhetki ||
Sakutan ghar betdi | na byahie Jivandas ||
Vahiko man rakhatan | hoy dharmako nash ||7||

|| Sakhi Shri Mukhki ||
Mit milave Jivana | rude na tadhun thay ||
Sukar kukarko besvo | rat divas mali gay ||8||
Kushal na puchhun Jivana | Harijan na aye dvar ||
Narak sam buro nahi | jam sami nahi dhar ||9||
Kamal na vikase Jivana | Harijan aye dvar ||
Bhath pado te manavi | kaha purush kaha nar ||10||
Chhatisun chhati mile | jake rude Harinam ||
Or duniyasun Jivana | apne kam bekam ||11||
Anin bhagatke jaiye | taj salilko sang ||
Anin majith rang Jivana | salil rang patang ||12||
Bhakti kare nav angsun | atam lang akhand ||
Mukti deuga Jivana | yun kahat hai Kamalakanth ||13||
Man kari kari Hari ochare | tan rahe kul pach manhi ||
Brahmadik bhule Jivana | so Harijan kahavat nahin ||14||
Ram upasi jo mile | tasun maliye dhay ||
An upasi Jivana | ta mukh dekhe balay ||15||
Bhakti kaisi Jivana | salil sakutan bhel ||
Jaise khara nirmen | pay diya sab thel ||16||
Kabahu bajave dakalun | kab ho baithe sadh ||
Nahi jami asmanmen | jaise untko pad ||17||

|| Iti Shri Salilka Ang sampurna ||18||
translation:
Here begins the Limb of the Salil (the half-hearted, divided devotee), 18.

1. Better a saakat (a godless, worldly man) than a salil, for the saakat may some day still cross over; the salil is sunk fast in the mire, O Jivana, like a boat left without water.

2. Let no one put faith in a salil devotee, O Jivana: one day he keeps satsang (holy company), the next day he goes off and mingles with the saakats.

3. An elephant sunk in mire has no hope of getting up again; flailing his hands, O Jivana, that servant drowns in the ocean of worldly existence.

4. In the Kanbi (farmer) caste, O Jivana, no line of true devotees is to be seen; they perform bhakti (devotion) for ten days and in the end come to [unclear].

5. The Bharado (Brahmin), the Kanbi and the Sonar (goldsmith) are no devotees, O Jivana; one or another turns out half-blind and half-formed, and if any is saved it is only by the Satguru's (true master's) grace.

6. Salil, saakat and Brahmin - they all stand jumbled together. This will never work, O Jivana, any more than raw castor oil becomes perfumed hair-oil.

|| The sakhi (couplet) of the meeting ||

7. Do not give a daughter in marriage into a saakat's house, O Jivandas; in keeping such a man's mind contented, one's own dharma is destroyed.

|| The sakhi from the holy mouth ||

8. Though glances meet, O Jivana, the heart does not grow cool by it; it is like the sitting together of a pig and a dog, mixing and howling night and day.

9. I ask after the welfare of no house, O Jivana, to whose door the harijan (devotee of Hari) does not come; there is nothing worse than hell, and no blade sharper than Yama's (death's).

10. If the lotus of the heart does not open, O Jivana, when a harijan comes to the door, into the furnace with that human being - be it a man or a woman.

11. Meet breast to breast with the one in whose heart is the name of Hari; with the rest of the world, O Jivana, our dealings are useless.

12. Go to the ananya (single-minded, exclusive) devotee and give up the company of the salil; the ananya's dye is the fast dye of madder, O Jivana, while the salil's colour is safflower that fades.

13. Do bhakti with all nine limbs of devotion, the soul unbrokenly attached: "I shall grant liberation," O Jivana - so says Kamalakanth (the Lord, husband of Lakshmi).

14. With his mind he utters Hari's name while his body stays bound in caste and family custom, and he strays away after Brahma and the other gods; such a man, O Jivana, is not to be called a harijan.

15. If a worshipper of Ram is met, run and embrace him; but one who worships another, O Jivana - to look upon his face is a calamity.

16. What sort of bhakti is this, O Jivana, mixed up with salils and saakats? It is like pouring milk into salt water - the whole of it is thrown away.

17. One moment he beats the dakalu (the little drum of goddess-rites), the next he sits as a sadhu; he is neither on the earth nor in the sky, O Jivana, but like a camel's wind.

|| Here ends the Limb of the Salil, 18. ||
